rationale: Packages hosts/manages private or public packages and dependencies with integrated permissions and FPT/GHEC billing. APIs, Actions and webhooks can support DevOps integration, but no actual integration, deployment or required universal centralization follows. The package metadata overview includes README, asserted license, version history and download statistics; these are not rights clearance, trusted provenance or verified package behavior. Registry-dependent permissions may inherit from a repository or be granular for personal/organization scope. Repository-based public visibility means GitHub-wide on cloud versus enterprise-wide otherwise; do not generalize to every registry or grant access. FPT/GHEC linked artifacts are metadata views of build/source/deployment information, not storage for package/image files. Upstream authoritative-metadata wording is not independent factual correctness or compliance proof; external registry use remains distinct from hosting in Packages. Cloud public packages are described as free; private included storage/transfer depend on plan. Without valid payment method quota exhaustion blocks usage; with one, budgets may limit spending. No present numeric price, actual budget or authorization to incur cost established. Client matrix associates JavaScript package.json with npm, Ruby Gemfile with gem, Java pom.xml with mvn, Gradle build.gradle/build.gradle.kts with gradle, .NET nupkg with dotnet CLI, and Dockerfile with Docker. This describes client formats, not installed tooling or permission to execute upstream builds. GHES legacy Docker subdomain isolation is strongly recommended, whereas Container Registry has required isolation reviewed elsewhere. GHEC with data residency lacks Maven and Gradle registries in this pinned guide; do not infer all GHEC or all registries unavailable. Authentication includes classic PAT scoped requirements plus explicit Actions GITHUB_TOKEN publication/read-access paths. GHEC managed-user product context permits organization namespaces, not personal publication. No tokens, grants or credentials changed. UI/REST deletion is described, while GraphQL private-version deletion applies only to eligible repository-permission registries and uses the same classic authentication PAT. Granular registries exclude Packages GraphQL; no universal deletion adapter, scope or approval inferred. Package webhooks can subscribe to publication/update events; this is not configured delivery, event completeness or receiver verification. No webhook created. Cloud feedback uses community discussions; documentation contradictions, unclear errors and sensitive published data direct users to Support. GHES support directs to site administrators. These are upstream routing suggestions, not authorization to disclose secrets/personal data or send messages. The comment-only GHES release-stage include supplies no stage; linked guides/specifications remain separate review work. No published revision assurance, policy acceptance, rights clearance or native enforcement established. Complete page and required include/feature/variable context inspected. Independent semantic/published assurance remains separate.
